publication: New Jersey Herald News (masthead: "combined with THE NEWARK HERALD"; billed as "New Jersey's Oldest Colored Weekly," Twelfth Year; published by Herald News Publishing Co., Inc.)
date: 1939-03-11 (Vol. XII, No. 5, week ending Saturday, March 11, 1939)
summary: 8-page Newark weekly. Front page covers the NJ State Temporary Commission report on discrimination against the state's 200,000+ Black residents, a Rutgers admissions-bias inquiry called a "whitewash," the Marian Anderson/DAR controversy reaching Newark, Elk leader Alfred Cooke's funeral, and a special series on conditions facing Negroes in NJ municipalities (starting with Newark). Inside: editorials on Sen. Bilbo's anti-intermarriage bill, church listings, statewide town correspondent columns (Ridgewood, Paterson, Rutherford, Long Branch, Roselle, Summit, Fair Haven, Kenilworth, Vaux Hall, Monmouth), a full society page, an amusements/clubs page (Nina Mae McKinney film "Gang Smashers" at the National Theatre), and sports (Lincoln-Morgan basketball, Henry Armstrong title defense in Havana, Negro National League baseball notes).

incidents.what: NJ State Temporary Commission on the Condition of the Urban Colored Population releases report finding systemic denial of citizenship rights to 200,000+ Black New Jerseyans; front-page editorial demands legislative and administrative action

Rutgers University accused, then publicly exonerated, of racially discriminatory admissions practices toward Ernest Baxter, prompting Essex County committee investigation branded a "whitewash" by Black citizens

Marian Anderson barred from Constitution Hall by DAR; Eleanor Roosevelt resigns from DAR in protest; Newark groups (James Weldon Johnson Literary Guild, New Era Democracy Club) organize telegram/support campaigns
Alfred Cooke, prominent Elk and church leader, dies and is buried following funeral at Bethany Baptist Church, Newark

Samuel W. Rushmore's offer of a $220,000 Plainfield estate as a maternity hospital for Negroes is refused by the hospital board; Rushmore's appointment to Jersey City Board of Freeholders opposed by Mayor Hague and Sen. Charles Loizeaux
Henry Armstrong retains welterweight title in Havana, knocking out Bobby Pancho in the 4th round

connections: Front page series "Obstacles Faced by the Race in Newark" is explicitly framed as first in a planned multi-part investigative series on conditions in NJ municipalities, continued inside and promising Jersey City next week

Roger M. Yancey identified as member of both the NJ Urban League Survey Commission and legal staff of the Newark Housing Authority, linking to Harold A. Lett (secretary of NJ Urban League, elected Housing Authority vice-chairman)

Masthead credits Herald News with statewide correspondents in principal NJ cities, evidenced by bylined town columns (Nathan O. Gumbs in Roselle/Passaic, Alice Wormley in Passaic, James Hendricks in Rutherford, Madeline Mumby in Long Branch, Kate Maney in Kenilworth, Neil Knight in Vaux Hall, Pauline Sears in Fair Haven, R. Stanford West in Summit)
Editorial "The Negro Press in New Jersey" explicitly positions the Herald News within a network of Black NJ papers advocating for civil rights coverage
